section_entries.label: Construction of Proposition 2's kernel
section_entries.mathematical_role: Builds a compactly supported smooth function by infinite convolution, proves transform decay from derivative bounds, and obtains strip positivity through a second convolution identity.

unit_result_entry.title: Infinite convolution gives compact support and subexponential transform decay
unit_result_entry.why_material: Constructs a smooth even nonnegative compactly supported function from scaled tents, derives factorial-logarithmic derivative bounds, and optimizes repeated integration by parts to obtain the required transform decay.

unit_dependency_entry.context_note: The final multiplication by a hyperbolic-secant factor preserves the needed spatial properties and strengthens the decay condition.
unit_dependency_entry.representation_dependency: High: derivative and Laplace-transform estimates (30)-(32) require formula recovery; prose preserves the construction.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Average zero density converted into an average-rank bound
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Uses kernel positivity to isolate central multiplicity, partitions off-center zeros by horizontal distance and height, inserts the density hypothesis, and optimizes the scale lambda as log D divided by log L(D).

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Strip positivity obtained through a transform convolution
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: Represents the final kernel transform as a convolution with the hyperbolic-secant transform and uses positivity of the first Fourier factor plus the sign of the real part of the second to prove the strip condition.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The kernel is designed backward from three downstream jobs--functional-equation symmetry, horizontal contour decay, and positivity for central multiplicity--then realized by infinite convolution and a positivity-preserving transform factor.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: The construction proves existence with sufficient decay and positivity; it does not claim optimality or uniqueness.
